cards.front: What should you know about graphic communication exam tips?
cards.back: Show the FLAT NET and the ASSEMBLED package. Test that your net actually folds — make a prototype. Consider sustainability — annotate material choices. Include all required information (barcode, contents, warnings).

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Packaging design is just about making the box look attractive. Correct: Packaging design must consider: PROTECTION (does it keep the product safe?), FUNCTION (does it open/close properly?), SUSTAINABILITY (materials, waste, recyclability), LEGISLATION (barcodes, ingredients, safety warnings), and aesthetics.
Design packaging for a product. Create the net, consider materials and sustainability, and design the surface graphics. Build a prototype and annotate your design decisions.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Packaging and Print Design
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Packaging and Print Design using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

Packaging serves four key functions: Protection (keeping the product safe during transport and storage), Containment (holding the product securely), Information (displaying legal requirements, ingredients, barcodes, and instructions), and Promotion (attracting customers at point of sale). Lithography (litho) prints high-quality, consistent colour in large quantities — ideal for magazines and packaging. Digital printing is cost-effective for short runs and personalisation. Screen printing suits thick inks on textiles and posters. Foil blocking applies metallic foil using heat and pressure for premium finishes. Embossing/debossing creates raised or recessed designs.
